coverage.note: Federal registry, staffing and stage evidence establish legal identity, incorporation, disclosed control bands and bounded workforce chronology.
The legal office, Etobicoke public address, Toronto engine facility and undisclosed test-site roles are separately documented.
The public mandate is bounded to R-1, R-2, E-1 and their shared launch and ground architecture.
R-series configuration and intended functions are documented, but payload and E-1 thrust baselines conflict and no versioned data sheet was located.
Facility and preliminary turbopump work are reported; completed component, hot-fire, licence, launch and flight outcomes are not public.
DND and NRC grants and the Controlled Goods listing are documented, but no procurement, customer service, accepted delivery or operational deployment is established.

attempts: Searched CanadaBuys, Transport Canada launch-licensing and public customer records; no CRC procurement award, launch licence, booking or manifested payload was located.
coverage.note: No CanadaBuys award, launch licence, customer booking or manifested payload attributable to CRC was located.
BDC's seed relationship and the DND and NRC funding events are separated by source, date and public basis.
The official homepage publishes the general public email and Etobicoke contact address.
The August 20 IEEE report provides a structured latest activity date and current R-2 development direction.
The candidate uses company, federal registry, DND, NRC, investor, parliamentary and independent industry source families.
R-2 payload and E-1 thrust figures remain explicitly conflicted rather than normalized into one design specification.

saturation.stopReason: The final bilingual, patent, procurement, launch-licensing, customer, site and technical-document probes added no new decision-changing proof beyond the Controlled Goods and IEEE records.

warnings: Current R-2 payload claims conflict across company, parliamentary and industry sources: 6,500 kilograms to 500-kilometre LEO, 12,500 kilograms with mixed or unstated orbit basis, and 12,000 to 15,000 kilograms to LEO; none is flight validated.
Current company-controlled E-1 descriptions vary between 700, 725 and 750 kilonewtons; no versioned data sheet or completed hot-fire result reconciles the design baseline.

No reviewed durable source establishes a completed component-test result, gas-generator or full-engine hot-fire, vehicle flight, launch licence, selected launch site, customer booking, manifested payload, accepted delivery or operational service.
DND agreement CO5-023 is a C$8,333,333 development grant tied to R1/light-lift work, not a procurement contract, completed prototype, flight, acceptance or fielding record.
NRC IRAP agreement 1041206 funds defence procurement and cybersecurity readiness; it does not establish procurement eligibility, certification, customer interest or successful project completion.

C$6.2 million, C$14.7 million, C$22.5 million and C$22.8 million figures use different dates and public bases; they are not summed, and exact current ownership percentages and the post-financing cap table remain undisclosed.
Telesat appears as payload-sizing context, not a customer, reservation or partner; reported test-site and launch-site arrangements remain undisclosed access or partnership discussions.
Controlled Goods Program registration is not a procurement award, product approval, security clearance, export authorization or evidence of eligibility for a specific acquisition.
